final.summary: Outfall pH stayed near neutral 7.08 to 7.58 with no excursions above 9, and the equalization tank level rose then fell during the treatment interval. After ETP inflow data returned at 2026-10-14 06:15, water balance and power versus load are within tolerance and outfall flow matches treated flow. Outfall flow rose to 80 to 91 m3/h from 2026-10-13 15:00 to 23:20 while conductivity fell with pH remaining neutral, indicating groundwater dilution of the outfall.

key_evidence.why: Outfall pH stayed neutral, ruling out raw alkaline discharge.
Outfall flow increased to 80-91 m3/h during 15:00-23:20.
Conductivity dropped during the flow increase with pH remaining neutral, indicating dilution.
Tank level rose then fell, consistent with holding then processing.
After S2 returned, ETP inflow, outfall and tank balance are within tolerance.
Power matches expected band for inflow after 06:15.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 14:00 to 2026-10-14 18:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
final.limitations: ETP inflow S2 is missing from 2026-10-13 14:00 to 2026-10-14 06:15, so treatment of the batch during the early part of the interval cannot be assessed from inflow. No accredited lab BOD results are available for the period. Dilution of the outfall means outfall readings do not represent the treated effluent alone.
final.unresolved: Whether the batch wastewater was actually processed through the ETP during the S2 gap, and whether the observed dilution was intentional tampering with the measurement point.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
